content.text:
**Finding: missing (high severity) — no customer termination-for-convenience right.**

- **§11.1** binds us to a five-year initial term with automatic one-year renewals; the only exit before expiry is the 30-day notice of non-renewal at term end.
- **§11.2** limits termination to uncured material breach and insolvency. No convenience right exists for either party anywhere in the agreement (other refund/termination triggers in §3, §7 and §8 are cause-based).
- Direction check: Commerce One also has no convenience right, so no vendor-side deletion is needed — that part already matches our preferred position.

**Redline (validated, ok:true):** new §11.4 inserted after §11.3 giving Corio a 30-day convenience termination (in whole or in part) with a refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, no early-termination fee or penalty, and express confirmation that Commerce One has no convenience right during the initial or any renewal term. Placement after §11.3 avoids renumbering the survival clause and its cross-references.
